assumptions: Assumption: Orthogonal intact-EV assays (capture + particle co-localization + detergent/protease protection) are sensitive and specific enough in program hands to detect source-dependent differences.
Assumption: Short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa sampling and capture from these matrices are technically feasible in the selected animal model.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 highlights source-cell dependence of EV composition and the need for orthogonal intact-EV assays. Rodent studies using MSC-derived conditioned medium show functional effects but do not link activity to a membrane-protected, intact-EV fraction. Senescence alters MSC secretome biology (SASP) and plausibly changes particle membrane integrity, surface phenotype, and cargo protection; these changes would undermine intact-EV identity, recoverability after intranasal delivery, and downstream potency-linkage assays.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Binary stratifier at lot generation: documented senescence-class (replicative-stable low p16/p21 vs induced SASP-rich) with orthogonal intact-EV analytic pass/fail correlation; not a numeric release test.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Source-cell senescence mechanism (replicative vs SASP-induced) as a required source qualification attribute
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Operationalizes a source-cell gate that, if predictive, de-risks downstream intact-EV identity, potency development, and cross-species bridging.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High-moderate: mechanistic plausibility exists but program-specific predictive value is unproven.

edges.competing_explanation: Culture conditions, donor genetics, or purification artifacts (not senescence) could drive observed compositional differences.
edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific orthogonal intact-EV comparison across senescence mechanisms with spike-in recovery controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV endorses source dependence and orthogonal analytics; rodent MSC-EV studies note source considerations but do not measure senescence mechanisms directly.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect intact-EV exposure in vivo may reflect administration, formulation, labeling sensitivity, or species-specific clearance rather than source-cell senescence per se.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched short-interval in vivo dosing and orthogonal intact-EV verification comparing materials from early- versus late-passage or induced-senescence MSCs.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: macaque intranasal biodistribution shows delivery risks; even if analytic signatures differ by source, formulation/administration/species clearance could confound in vivo recoverability.

nodes.statement: Donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative-passage low p16/p21 versus SASP-rich induced senescence) determines features of released particle populations (membrane integrity, surface-markers, particle:protein ratio).

These senescence-linked particle features produce distinct orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures: capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive versus marker signal that tracks with bulk soluble protein and is detergent-insensitive.

Materials with the senescence-favorable intact-EV signature are more likely to yield short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing than materials from senescent/SASP-rich MSC sources.

competing_explanations: Differences in observed intact-EV signatures could result from upstream culture conditions, donor-to-donor genetic variation, media composition, or fractionation artifacts rather than senescence mechanism.
In vivo lack of recovery might be driven by administration/labeling/formulation factors or species clearance independent of source-cell-dependent EV integrity.
dependencies: Establish validated exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and capture-compatibility panels prior to interpretation
Generate >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots per senescence class from the same donor(s) where feasible
Optimize short-interval sampling and low-biomass capture from nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa
design_question: Daily question: Does the donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative-passage low-p16/p21 versus SASP-rich induced senescence) causally change the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature in conditioned-medium-derived preparations and the short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa recoverable intact-EV signal after matched intranasal dosing?
expected_measurable_effect: Conditioned medium from early-passage, low-p16/p21 MSCs will reproducibly show: (A) an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) in bounded fractions, and (B) detectable capture-positive and particle evidence in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after matched intranasal dosing; materials from SASP-rich/late-passage sources will not reproducibly show these features.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow: (1) density/SEC fractionation with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture on intact fractions for canonical markers and separate spike-in tracer readout; (3) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material; (4) short-interval in vivo sampling and orthogonal capture/particle verification from lavage/CSF/tissue.
experiment.comparator: Within-donor matched comparisons across senescence states: bounded small-EV fraction from early-passage baseline MSCs versus bounded fractions from replicative-passage senescent and induced SASP-rich senescent MSCs; include secretome-retaining controls and membrane-disrupted aliquots.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation spiked and processed in parallel (validates capture/protection assays). Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Spike-in tracer per-sample recovery control required.
dependencies: Robust senescence-state characterization (p16/p21 qPCR or protein, SASP protein panel) per lot
Analytical capability for low-biomass orthogonal capture from lavage/CSF and validated spike-in tracer availability
Animal protocol and ethical approvals for short-interval sampling
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible difference between senescence mechanisms across replicates in orthogonal intact-EV signatures or in short-interval in vivo recoverability despite validated spike-in recovery, or inconsistent spike-in recovery preventing controlled discrimination.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, do not adopt senescence mechanism as a deterministic source-cell gate; pivot to alternative source/process variables or secretome-centric product definitions. If spike-in control fails, redesign control/assay before concluding on senescence effects.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Conditioned medium from early-passage, low p16/p21 MSCs will yield an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and greater short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after matched intranasal dosing compared with conditioned medium from late-passage or SASP-induced MSCs.
experiment.primary_readout: Co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase in conditioned-medium-derived preparations; presence and relative magnitude of capture-positive signal and particle counts in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing comparing senescence states.
experiment.question: Does donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative low p16/p21 versus SASP-rich induced senescence) causally alter the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature in conditioned-medium-derived preparations and short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence after matched intranasal dosing?
required_material: Donor-matched MSC cultures expanded to produce: (A) early-passage, low p16/p21 lots; (B) late-passage, high p16/p21 lots; and (C) induced SASP-rich senescent lots (oxidative stress/irradiation) where feasible

Conditioned medium from each source-cell lot processed identically into: (1) enriched small-EV preparation (program-defined bounded fraction) and (2) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining)
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) for per-sample recovery control
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane-disruption controls
Short-interval in vivo rodent dosing capability with ability to collect nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue at predefined short post-dose intervals
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not)
Protected-cargo panel presence/absence in capture-positive fractions (optional)
Reproducibility across biological replicates (>=3 lots per senescence condition)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent donor-matched preparations, early-passage low-p16/p21 derived materials reproducibly show (A) capture-positive particle-peak co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal in source material and (B) detectable capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in short-interval lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing; contrasting senescence mechanisms reproducibly fail these criteria under identical processing and dosing.

explicit_inferences: Inference: Senescence mechanism may change membrane integrity and surface phenotype leading to loss of orthogonal intact-EV signature despite similar bulk particle counts.
Inference: If source-cell senescence gates are adopted, downstream assay development and cross-species bridging will be less likely to be confounded by unrecognized source-cell variability.
falsification_criteria: Failure to observe reproducible difference across >=3 independent biological lots: early-passage low-p16/p21 materials do not consistently show co-localized capture+particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal while late-passage or induced SASP lots do.

Failure to detect orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing for the putative favorable senescence class despite validated spike-in recovery (i.e., analytic methods work but exposure is absent).

If either falsification condition is met, senescence mechanism must not be used as a deterministic source-cell gate; program should pivot to alternative source/process variables or secretome-centric strategies.
human_decisions_required: Select specific senescence operationalization metrics (p16/p21 thresholds, SASP panel components and induction protocol)
Approve animal sampling window and ethical protocols for short-interval recovery
Allocate resources for spike-in reagent qualification and orthogonal assay harmonization
manufacturability_assessment: Operationalizing a senescence-mechanism gate requires MCB/WCB strategies that preserve the chosen senescence phenotype, in-process senescence monitoring (p16/p21 assays, SASP panels), and capacity to produce >=3 independent lots per class for assay reproducibility. These steps are feasible but will require upstream process control and additional CMC effort.
manufacturing_rationale: Defining a source-cell senescence-mechanism gate will focus MCB/WCB selection, reduce lot-to-lot variability risk, and make downstream orthogonal QC, potency assay development, and scale-up evaluation interpretable. Without such a gate, analytical failures or negative large-animal biodistribution could waste bridging resources.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal analytics on matched conditioned-medium lots: immuno-capture of intact material (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) combined with density/SEC fractionation and particle counting (NTA/TRPS) to document co-localization; detergent + protease + RNase protection to confirm membrane protection; per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in to validate recovery. Short-interval in vivo sampling (rodent) of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa followed by same orthogonal capture to verify in vivo recoverability.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis uniquely operationalizes MSC senescence mechanism (replicative versus SASP-rich induced) as an explicit source-cell qualification gate tied to orthogonal intact-EV analytics plus short-interval in vivo recoverability. Prior source-cell hypotheses in this program examined senescence-associated variables (passage number, p16/p21) and suggested source dependence, but none combine (A) a mechanistic distinction of senescence mechanism, (B) a per-sample spike-in-controlled orthogonal intact-EV identity workflow, and (C) a matched short-interval intranasal in vivo→ex vivo recoverability test as a single discriminating decision gate. This integrated in vitro→in vivo test is thus genuinely new relative to earlier hypothesis iterations.
principal_risks: Risk that spike-in and orthogonal assays lack sensitivity in low-biomass lavage/CSF samples, yielding false negatives.
Risk that senescence mechanism is not the dominant driver of analytical variability; gating on it could discard usable lots.
Risk that preserving an intact-EV signature is necessary but not sufficient for cross-species intranasal CNS exposure; bridges may still fail due to route/formulation/species factors.
proposed_potency_relationship: If supported, an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected attribute (co-localizing capture+particle peak and detergent/protease-sensitive protected-cargo) will be linked to short-interval ex vivo PD readouts and thus become the potency-relevant identity-linked attribute for lots from the approved senescence class.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a source-cell qualification gate: require donor-MSCs to be characterized by senescence mechanism (replicative-passage low p16/p21 versus SASP-rich induced senescence) and advance only lots from the senescence-mechanism class that reproducibly yield an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal) and detectable short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence after intranasal dosing.
title: Hypothesis SGL-001-SC-001: Donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative versus SASP-rich induced) causally determines intact-EV analytical signature and short-interval intranasal recoverability
